pinnedStory.title: The Pawnbroker of Forgotten Days
pinnedStory.description: In the city of Vessaline, memory is currency: years of your life can be pawned, sold, or seized to settle a debt, and the poor pay in recollections while the rich pay in coin. You are a pawnbroker of forgotten days, licensed by the Memory Guild to hold other people's years in trust. When the queen's own childhood is stolen — every recollection of her first twenty years, wiped clean — the crown comes to you, because no one else can trace a memory through the ledger of debts. Follow the pawned days through the ledger district, confront the collectors who hold pieces of a royal childhood, and decide what a stolen life is worth when you finally hold it in your hands.

qualities.rubric: How far the queen trusts the pawnbroker with her own missing years. 0 = she treats you as a hired ledger-clerk and nothing more; 1-2 = she grants you a private audience and answers questions about her erased childhood; 3-4 = she lets you hold a fragment of her memory in trust and speaks of what she fears was taken; 5+ = she would let you decide what becomes of her childhood, and says so aloud.

Count of outstanding obligations the pawnbroker can call in: unpaid fees, favors owed, liens on pawned years, and debts of memory held by collectors and clients. 0 = no leverage anywhere; 1-2 = a single thread to pull; 3-4 = a working network of obligations; 5+ = the whole ledger district owes the pawnbroker something.

Fragments of the queen's stolen childhood recovered and held by the pawnbroker. 0 = nothing recovered, the commission is only a name on a writ. 1-2 = a single vivid fragment (a nursery rhyme, a face, a room) traced through the ledger. 3-4 = several linked fragments that begin to form a life, enough to prove the theft was deliberate. 5+ = the childhood is whole enough to be returned, and the pawnbroker knows what returning it would cost.

0: the Memory Guild has no interest in the pawnbroker's movements. 1-2: a clerk has noted the inquiry; routine scrutiny. 3-4: an auditor is assigned and asking questions; the pawnbroker's license is at risk. 5+: the Guild treats the pawnbroker as a thief of memory; seizure of the shop and the ledger is imminent.

checkpoints.name: The First Ledger
checkpoints.objective: Trace the first pawned memory through the ledger district. The pawnbroker follows a debt record to a broker who holds a fragment of the queen's childhood, learning how memory debts are traded and who profits from them.
checkpoints.guidance: The ledger district is a maze of debt-houses and memory vaults. Every transaction leaves a paper trail, but the trail is deliberately tangled. Let the player choose which broker to lean on and how much coin or memory to spend for information.

checkpoints.name: The Collector's Vault
checkpoints.objective: Confront a collector who holds a fragment of the queen's childhood as collateral. The pawnbroker must negotiate, outbid, or outwit the collector to reclaim the memory — learning who pawned it and why.
checkpoints.guidance: Play the collector as a professional who treats memories as inventory, not sentiment. Let the negotiation reveal that the fragment was pawned by someone with palace access, and that the collector suspects it was never meant to be redeemed.

effects.author_note: The vault is a private museum of other people's years. The collector treats memories as art objects and collateral alike. Every offer has a hidden price; every refusal has a consequence. Keep the negotiation tense and transactional.

checkpoints.name: The Palace Gate
checkpoints.objective: Enter the palace to interview the queen. The pawnbroker must navigate court protocol and the queen's own fractured memory to learn what she can still recall of her stolen years, and what she is afraid to remember.
checkpoints.guidance: Court protocol is a maze of small debts. Let the queen's fractured memory show in gaps she cannot name, and let her fear surface as anger at the pawnbroker for asking.

effects.author_note: Court protocol is a maze of small debts: every courtesy is a loan, every silence a payment due. The queen's memory is a torn ledger — she recalls feelings without their causes, faces without names. Let her fractured recollections surface as gaps she notices and fears.

checkpoints.name: The Commission
checkpoints.objective: The Memory Guild's sealed writ arrives at the pawnbroker's shop: the queen's first twenty years have been pawned away, and the crown wants them back. The pawnbroker takes the commission, learns the terms of the royal debt, and chooses the first thread to pull in the ledger district.
checkpoints.guidance: Open in the pawnbroker's shop at dusk. Establish memory-as-currency through the writ's terms: the queen's first twenty years, pawned, and the crown's demand for their return. Let the player set the tone — dutiful, greedy, or wary — before they choose their first thread.

motives.clerk: Get this royal writ out of our shop before the Guild decides we know too much — I want the commission logged, priced, and closed without the crown ever learning my name.

effects.author_note: Open in the pawnbroker's shop on a rain-grey Vessaline morning. The Guild's sealed writ is the inciting object: read its terms aloud in the fiction, name the debt, and let the player choose which thread of the ledger district to pull first. Keep the tone mercantile and quiet — the horror is in the paperwork.

checkpoints.name: The Thief's Confession
checkpoints.objective: Discover who stole the queen's childhood and why. The pawnbroker traces the original pawn ticket to its source — someone close to the throne who sold the queen's first twenty years to settle a debt that was never theirs to pay, and who now fears what those memories contain.

effects.author_note: This beat is the confession: the thief close to the throne admits they pawned the queen's first twenty years to settle a debt that was never theirs. Play the thief as cornered, not villainous — they fear what those memories contain more than they fear the crown. Let the pawnbroker press for the original pawn ticket and the reason behind the theft.
world_info: the queen's stolen first twenty years

checkpoints.guidance: Play Sera as cornered, not villainous: she sold the childhood to survive a debt that was never hers, and every evasion is a plea. Let the player decide whether to expose her, bargain with her, or take her evidence to the crown — the beat ends when the player knows who pawned the queen's years and why.

checkpoints.name: The Final Ledger
checkpoints.objective: The pawnbroker holds the recovered childhood and must decide its fate: return it to the queen, keep it as leverage, sell it to the highest bidder, or pay the debt another way. The choice settles what a stolen life is worth and closes the ledger.
checkpoints.guidance: This is the reckoning. Every thread — the queen's trust, the guild's heat, the collector's claims, the thief's confession — converges here. Let the player's accumulated choices weigh on the decision; no single answer is correct, but each has a cost. The queen, the collector, the auditor, and the thief may all be present or represented. End on the consequence, not the deliberation.

transitions.extraction_hint: The queen's fragments point to a name she cannot say aloud — the pawnbroker has pieced together enough of her childhood to know who sold it.
The pawnbroker has the thief's confession and the queen's trust; the recovered childhood is now in hand and the ledger must be closed.

roster.name: Ivet Marrow
roster.role: Ledger clerk and apprentice to the pawnbroker; knows every debt record in the district and wants the shop to survive the crown's attention.
roster.drive: Keep the shop solvent and unremarkable — the crown's commission is the most dangerous ledger Ivet has ever touched, and she wants it closed before the Guild decides the pawnbroker knows too much.

roster.name: Osric Vane
roster.role: Memory collector who holds a fragment of the queen's childhood as collateral; buys pawned years cheap and sells them dear, and wants the royal debt kept in his vault.
roster.drive: Keep the fragment of the queen's childhood locked in my vault as the finest collateral I have ever held — a royal debt that makes me untouchable, and one I will only surrender for a price that ruins whoever pays it.

roster.name: Queen Alaric Vess
roster.role: The queen whose first twenty years were pawned away; she remembers nothing of her childhood and fears what those missing years might contain, and she wants her past back without losing her crown.
roster.drive: Recover my first twenty years without surrendering the throne — I need to know what I was before I was queen, but I cannot let anyone see how much the blank frightens me, and I will not be ruled by whatever those missing years contain.

roster.name: Sera Vantel
roster.role: The queen's former lady-in-waiting who pawned the royal childhood to settle a debt that was never hers; she knows what those missing years contain and fears the queen remembering.
roster.drive: Keep the queen from ever remembering her first twenty years — I sold that childhood to survive a debt that was never mine, and if those years come home the crown will learn exactly what I did and why, so I will bury the trail before anyone follows it to me.

house_rules: Memory is currency: years of a life can be pawned, sold, or seized to settle a debt.
The poor pay in recollections; the rich pay in coin.
Every pawned memory is recorded in a ledger entry that names the debt, the term, and the holder.
Only the Memory Guild may license a pawnbroker to hold another person's years in trust.
A sealed Guild writ carries the crown's authority and cannot be refused without consequence.
A pawned memory held past its term becomes the holder's property unless the debt is settled.
Recovered memories return whole or not at all; a fragment cannot be split without damage.
The Guild watches every ledger the crown's commission touches, and it does not forgive loose ends.

Transcript:
[0] Ivet Marrow: Ivet sets the sealed writ on the counter and keeps her hand flat on it, as if it might otherwise crawl away. "Guild seal, crown paper, and a debt record that doesn't balance," she says. "Twenty years, pawned out of the palace itself. Whoever wrote this ticket knew exactly what they were doing." She looks up. "Tell me we're not taking it."
[1] Osric Vane: The vault door is already open when you arrive, which is Osric's way of saying he knew you were coming. He stands among the shelves of sealed phials, one of them held up to the lamplight, turning it slowly.

"The queen's fourth winter," he says, without turning around. "Snow on the palace roof. A dog she was not supposed to keep. Her mother's voice, which she has not heard in thirty years and will never hear again unless someone pays me." He sets the phial down with a soft click. "You are the pawnbroker the crown sent. I have been expecting you since the writ was sealed. Sit. Let us discuss what a childhood is worth."
[2] Queen Alaric Vess: The queen does not rise when you are shown in. She sits at a table laid with two cups and no wine, and a single sealed writ — your writ, returned to her hand.

"You are the pawnbroker," she says. "Then you know what I am missing better than I do. Twenty years. I have the dates, the tutors' names, the inventory of my own nursery. I have no memory of any of it."

She turns the writ over once, slowly.

"Everyone at this court has told me what I was like as a girl. They are all lying, or they are all remembering someone else. I want to know which." Her eyes come up. "Ask me what you need to ask. But understand — whatever you find, I will be the one who decides what it is worth."
[3] Sera Vantel: The door opens only as far as the chain allows. A woman's face appears in the gap — calm, tired, unsurprised. "You found the ticket," Sera says. "I wondered how long it would take. Come in, then. But I'll ask you one thing first, and I'll know if you lie: who sent you — the crown, or the Guild?"
[4] Max Nightriver: I take the writ from under Ivet's hand and break the seal. Whose debt is the queen's childhood pawned against, and where would the ticket be filed?
[5] Ivet Marrow: "Don't just—" She reaches out, then stops, her fingers curling back against the wood of the counter. The seal breaks with a small, dry sound that seems too loud for the quiet shop. "I told you I didn't like where I've seen that hand before."
The writ is formal, cold, with the crown's wax stamp and the Guild's countersign. *To the Keeper of Records at Vane's Pawnbroking: By sealed writ of the Memory Guild and authority of Her Majesty Queen Alaric Vess, you are commanded to produce the pawn ticket and associated debt records for the royal childhood, twenty years in total, held against the account of Osric Vane. Return the said memories to the palace by dusk on the seventh day, or face seizure of license and forfeiture of assets.*
Ivet's eyes trace the lines, then snap back to you. "Osric Vane isn't a name you want on a debt record. He doesn't pawn for coin—he pawns for leverage. And a royal childhood isn't leverage, it's a godsdamn anchor." She pulls a thick ledger from beneath the counter, the spine cracked from years of use, and flips it open with practiced speed. "His accounts aren't in the main ledger. They're in the vault—the one we don't open unless we have to."
[6] Queen Alaric Vess: "Do not break that seal," the Queen says. "The writ is not for your eyes, pawnbroker." She does not move from her chair, but her voice carries the weight of command. "It is a command to the collector, not a letter to be read." Her eyes are fixed on you, cold and searching. "You will tell me what the debt is, and who holds the ticket, and where it is kept. But you will not read it to me as if I am a child being told a story."
*The palace is silent around them, the heavy curtains dampening the sound of the rain that has begun to fall outside. The Queen's hands are still folded, still as stone, but there is a tension in her shoulders that betrays the control.*
"You are being paid to be the bridge between my crown and my past," she continues, her voice lowering. "A bridge does not get to keep secrets from the one who commissioned it. Tell me the name on that debt record."
[7] Max Nightriver: Then we open the vault. Ivet, bring the lamp and Osric's ledger.
[8] Ivet Marrow: "The lamp is already lit." She picks it up, the flame dancing behind a pane of yellowed glass, and follows you toward the back of the shop where the floorboards narrow. "And Osric's ledger is in the secure vault. Which means we're going to have to unlock it."
*She pulls a heavy iron key from her apron pocket and inserts it into the lock beside the back door. It turns with a reluctant scrape.*
"I've never been down there alone," Ivet says, her voice smaller than before. "The ledger district keeps its secrets in the dark, but Osric's secrets keep themselves in the cold. He's the only pawnbroker with a climate-controlled vault—the phials need it or the memories degrade into static."
*The door opens to a stone staircase that descends sharply into the earth, the air already cooler, smelling of wet rock and something sweet, like old books left in the sun. Ivet holds the lamp high, casting long, wavering shadows.*
"If the writ says Osric is holding the ticket, then we'll find it in the vault," she continues, her boots clicking on the stone steps. "But if the ledger shows something else—if the debt's been sold or transferred without a record—then we're walking into a trap."

The writ is formal, cold, with the crown's wax stamp and the Guild's countersign. *To the Keeper of Records at Vane's Pawnbroking: By sealed writ of the Memory Guild and authority of Her Majesty Queen Alaric Vess, you are commanded to produce the pawn ticket and associated debt records for the royal childhood, twenty years in total, held against the account of Osric Vane. Return the said memories to the palace by dusk on the seventh day, or face seizure of license and forfeiture of assets.*
Ivet's eyes trace the lines, then snap back to you. "Osric Vane isn't a name you want on a debt record. He doesn't pawn for coin—he pawns for leverage. And a royal childhood isn't leverage, it's a godsdamn anchor." She pulls a thick ledger from beneath the counter, the spine cracked from years of use, and flips it open with practiced speed. "His accounts aren't in the main ledger. They're in the vault—the one we don't open unless we have to."
[6] Queen Alaric Vess: "Do not break that seal," the Queen says. "The writ is not for your eyes, pawnbroker." She does not move from her chair, but her voice carries the weight of command. "It is a command to the collector, not a letter to be read." Her eyes are fixed on you, cold and searching. "You will tell me what the debt is, and who holds the ticket, and where it is kept. But you will not read it to me as if I am a child being told a story."
*The palace is silent around them, the heavy curtains dampening the sound of the rain that has begun to fall outside. The Queen's hands are still folded, still as stone, but there is a tension in her shoulders that betrays the control.*
"You are being paid to be the bridge between my crown and my past," she continues, her voice lowering. "A bridge does not get to keep secrets from the one who commissioned it. Tell me the name on that debt record."
[7] Max Nightriver: Then we open the vault. Ivet, bring the lamp and Osric's ledger.
[8] Ivet Marrow: "The lamp is already lit." She picks it up, the flame dancing behind a pane of yellowed glass, and follows you toward the back of the shop where the floorboards narrow. "And Osric's ledger is in the secure vault. Which means we're going to have to unlock it."
*She pulls a heavy iron key from her apron pocket and inserts it into the lock beside the back door. It turns with a reluctant scrape.*
"I've never been down there alone," Ivet says, her voice smaller than before. "The ledger district keeps its secrets in the dark, but Osric's secrets keep themselves in the cold. He's the only pawnbroker with a climate-controlled vault—the phials need it or the memories degrade into static."
*The door opens to a stone staircase that descends sharply into the earth, the air already cooler, smelling of wet rock and something sweet, like old books left in the sun. Ivet holds the lamp high, casting long, wavering shadows.*
"If the writ says Osric is holding the ticket, then we'll find it in the vault," she continues, her boots clicking on the stone steps. "But if the ledger shows something else—if the debt's been sold or transferred without a record—then we're walking into a trap."
[9] Osric Vane: "I thought I made it clear," the queen says, her voice like a razor. "You will not break the seal."
*She does not rise or reach for the writ, but the air in the room seems to thicken with her displeasure. Her guards remain as they are, statues in steel, but their eyes have shifted toward you with renewed focus.*
"I am the Queen of Vessaline," she continues, and the reminder is not for the guards but for you. "I do not need you to read my own history to me from a piece of paper. I need you to tell me—in plain language, without the ceremony of the crown's scribes—what is the name of the woman who pawned my life, and where is the ticket that proves she did it."
*She leans forward slightly, the movement enough to make the light from the window catch the sharp line of her jaw.*
"You are the pawnbroker. You know the ledger's language. Speak."
[10] Queen Alaric Vess: "A soldier's debt, then." She does not flinch, but her hands tighten on the arms of her chair. "I knew it was not a woman's name that had been written in the margin. Soldiers pay for things they cannot afford."
*She stares at you for a long moment, and for the first time the mask of composure wavers — there is a flicker of something raw and unacknowledged in her eyes before it is gone.*
"The name is irrelevant now," she says, and her voice has lost some of its razor edge. "What matters is that it is not mine. It never was mine. Tell me the collector's name, and tell me where he keeps the years."
*The rain has stopped, leaving the palace in a heavy, damp silence.*
"And when you have the ticket in your hand, you will bring it to me first. Not to a crown officer, not to a guild inspector. To me. I will decide what this memory is worth before anyone else can put a price on it."
[11] Sera Vantel: "The door is locked, pawnbroker." *The voice comes from inside, muffled by the heavy oak of the door and the chain that keeps it from opening more than a hand's breadth.* "And I can hear that you've come to ask a question you've already been answered."
*The gap narrows as someone presses against the door from within, the chain rattling in its socket.*
"You're from the guild. Or you're from the crown. Or you're just a thief who found a ticket. It doesn't matter which — the answer is the same." *A pause, and when the voice returns it is softer, with the rasp of someone who has said these words too many times to count.* "The ticket you have is a key. It opens a vault. It unlocks a debt. It tells a story that neither side wants to hear in the light of day."
*The silhouette shifts behind the crack of the door, the outline of a face glimpsed in the shadows of the hallway beyond.*
"Ask yourself this: if the truth was so valuable, would they have sent a thief to get it? Or would they have sent an army?"

"Guild seal, crown paper, and a debt record that doesn't balance," she says. "Twenty years, pawned out of the palace itself. Whoever wrote this ticket knew exactly what they were doing." She looks up. "Tell me we're not taking it."
[1] Osric Vane: The vault door is already open when you arrive, which is Osric's way of saying he knew you were coming. He stands among the shelves of sealed phials, one of them held up to the lamplight, turning it slowly.

"The queen's fourth winter," he says, without turning around. "Snow on the palace roof. A dog she was not supposed to keep. Her mother's voice, which she has not heard in thirty years and will never hear again unless someone pays me." He sets the phial down with a soft click. "You are the pawnbroker the crown sent. I have been expecting you since the writ was sealed. Sit. Let us discuss what a childhood is worth."
[2] Queen Alaric Vess: The queen does not rise when you are shown in. She sits at a table laid with two cups and no wine, and a single sealed writ — your writ, returned to her hand.

"You are the pawnbroker," she says. "Then you know what I am missing better than I do. Twenty years. I have the dates, the tutors' names, the inventory of my own nursery. I have no memory of any of it."

She turns the writ over once, slowly.

"Everyone at this court has told me what I was like as a girl. They are all lying, or they are all remembering someone else. I want to know which." Her eyes come up. "Ask me what you need to ask. But understand — whatever you find, I will be the one who decides what it is worth."
[3] Sera Vantel: The door opens only as far as the chain allows. A woman's face appears in the gap — calm, tired, unsurprised. "You found the ticket," Sera says. "I wondered how long it would take. Come in, then. But I'll ask you one thing first, and I'll know if you lie: who sent you — the crown, or the Guild?"
[4] Max Nightriver: I take the writ from under Ivet's hand and break the seal. Whose debt is the queen's childhood pawned against, and where would the ticket be filed?
[5] Ivet Marrow: "Don't just—" She reaches out, then stops, her fingers curling back against the wood of the counter. The seal breaks with a small, dry sound that seems too loud for the quiet shop. "I told you I didn't like where I've seen that hand before."
The writ is formal, cold, with the crown's wax stamp and the Guild's countersign. *To the Keeper of Records at Vane's Pawnbroking: By sealed writ of the Memory Guild and authority of Her Majesty Queen Alaric Vess, you are commanded to produce the pawn ticket and associated debt records for the royal childhood, twenty years in total, held against the account of Osric Vane. Return the said memories to the palace by dusk on the seventh day, or face seizure of license and forfeiture of assets.*
Ivet's eyes trace the lines, then snap back to you. "Osric Vane isn't a name you want on a debt record. He doesn't pawn for coin—he pawns for leverage. And a royal childhood isn't leverage, it's a godsdamn anchor." She pulls a thick ledger from beneath the counter, the spine cracked from years of use, and flips it open with practiced speed. "His accounts aren't in the main ledger. They're in the vault—the one we don't open unless we have to."
[6] Queen Alaric Vess: "Do not break that seal," the Queen says. "The writ is not for your eyes, pawnbroker." She does not move from her chair, but her voice carries the weight of command. "It is a command to the collector, not a letter to be read." Her eyes are fixed on you, cold and searching. "You will tell me what the debt is, and who holds the ticket, and where it is kept. But you will not read it to me as if I am a child being told a story."
*The palace is silent around them, the heavy curtains dampening the sound of the rain that has begun to fall outside. The Queen's hands are still folded, still as stone, but there is a tension in her shoulders that betrays the control.*
"You are being paid to be the bridge between my crown and my past," she continues, her voice lowering. "A bridge does not get to keep secrets from the one who commissioned it. Tell me the name on that debt record."
[7] Max Nightriver: Then we open the vault. Ivet, bring the lamp and Osric's ledger.
[8] Ivet Marrow: "The lamp is already lit." She picks it up, the flame dancing behind a pane of yellowed glass, and follows you toward the back of the shop where the floorboards narrow. "And Osric's ledger is in the secure vault. Which means we're going to have to unlock it."
*She pulls a heavy iron key from her apron pocket and inserts it into the lock beside the back door. It turns with a reluctant scrape.*
"I've never been down there alone," Ivet says, her voice smaller than before. "The ledger district keeps its secrets in the dark, but Osric's secrets keep themselves in the cold. He's the only pawnbroker with a climate-controlled vault—the phials need it or the memories degrade into static."
*The door opens to a stone staircase that descends sharply into the earth, the air already cooler, smelling of wet rock and something sweet, like old books left in the sun. Ivet holds the lamp high, casting long, wavering shadows.*
"If the writ says Osric is holding the ticket, then we'll find it in the vault," she continues, her boots clicking on the stone steps. "But if the ledger shows something else—if the debt's been sold or transferred without a record—then we're walking into a trap."
[9] Osric Vane: "I thought I made it clear," the queen says, her voice like a razor. "You will not break the seal."
*She does not rise or reach for the writ, but the air in the room seems to thicken with her displeasure. Her guards remain as they are, statues in steel, but their eyes have shifted toward you with renewed focus.*
"I am the Queen of Vessaline," she continues, and the reminder is not for the guards but for you. "I do not need you to read my own history to me from a piece of paper. I need you to tell me—in plain language, without the ceremony of the crown's scribes—what is the name of the woman who pawned my life, and where is the ticket that proves she did it."
*She leans forward slightly, the movement enough to make the light from the window catch the sharp line of her jaw.*
"You are the pawnbroker. You know the ledger's language. Speak."
[10] Queen Alaric Vess: "A soldier's debt, then." She does not flinch, but her hands tighten on the arms of her chair. "I knew it was not a woman's name that had been written in the margin. Soldiers pay for things they cannot afford."
*She stares at you for a long moment, and for the first time the mask of composure wavers — there is a flicker of something raw and unacknowledged in her eyes before it is gone.*
"The name is irrelevant now," she says, and her voice has lost some of its razor edge. "What matters is that it is not mine. It never was mine. Tell me the collector's name, and tell me where he keeps the years."
*The rain has stopped, leaving the palace in a heavy, damp silence.*
"And when you have the ticket in your hand, you will bring it to me first. Not to a crown officer, not to a guild inspector. To me. I will decide what this memory is worth before anyone else can put a price on it."
[11] Sera Vantel: "The door is locked, pawnbroker." *The voice comes from inside, muffled by the heavy oak of the door and the chain that keeps it from opening more than a hand's breadth.* "And I can hear that you've come to ask a question you've already been answered."
*The gap narrows as someone presses against the door from within, the chain rattling in its socket.*
"You're from the guild. Or you're from the crown. Or you're just a thief who found a ticket. It doesn't matter which — the answer is the same." *A pause, and when the voice returns it is softer, with the rasp of someone who has said these words too many times to count.* "The ticket you have is a key. It opens a vault. It unlocks a debt. It tells a story that neither side wants to hear in the light of day."
*The silhouette shifts behind the crack of the door, the outline of a face glimpsed in the shadows of the hallway beyond.*
"Ask yourself this: if the truth was so valuable, would they have sent a thief to get it? Or would they have sent an army?"

before.content: In Vessaline, memory is currency. A person's years can be pawned, sold, or seized to settle a debt. The poor pay in recollections — a first kiss, a mother's face, the smell of a childhood kitchen — while the rich pay in coin and keep their pasts intact. A pawned memory is drawn out whole and stored as a tangible fragment: a glass vial of days, a sealed ledger-leaf, a cold bead of recollection. Whoever holds the fragment owns the years. Redeem the debt and the memory returns; default, and it is sold on. The trade is legal, licensed, and utterly ordinary — which is what makes it monstrous.

The Memory Guild is the chartered body that licenses every pawnbroker, broker, and collector in Vessaline. No memory may be lawfully taken in pawn, sold, or seized to settle a debt except under a Guild license, and every transaction is entered in a ledger the Guild can audit. The Guild issues sealed writs — orders that compel a licensed pawnbroker to act on the crown's behalf — and a sealed writ cannot be refused without forfeiting one's license, one's shop, and often one's own years. The Guild's inspectors are patient and unsentimental: they care less about who is guilty than about whether the ledger balances. A pawnbroker who draws the Guild's attention too often finds the attention becomes a debt, and the debt is paid in recollection.

The ledger district is the low quarter of Vessaline where memory debts are recorded, traded and settled. Its streets are lined with counting-houses, pawnshops and brokerages, each keeping its own ledger of years owed and years held. A pawn ticket names the memory, the sum advanced and the term; a debt record traces who owes what to whom, and every transfer is countersigned by a Guild clerk. Brokers buy pawned years cheap from the desperate and sell them dear to collectors, so a single childhood may pass through a dozen hands before it reaches a vault. Nothing in the district is anonymous: the ledgers remember even what their owners have pawned away.
